accepted.s: The net sown area of Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25 was 59.14 lakh hectares. This represented what percentage of the total area of 162.97 lakh hectares?
accepted.x: The net sown area of 59.14 lakh hectares constituted 36.29% of the total area of 162.97 lakh hectares.
accepted.tq: Match the area figure with its stated percentage instead of estimating from unrelated irrigation figures.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the irrigation indicators for Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24?
o: GIA 36.77 lakh ha, NIA 26.03 lakh ha and cropping intensity 1.88
GIA 32.71 lakh ha, NIA 30.33 lakh ha and cropping intensity 1.21
GIA 36.56 lakh ha, NIA 28.56 lakh ha and cropping intensity 1.88
GIA 32.71 lakh ha, NIA 26.03 lakh ha and cropping intensity 1.21
accepted.x: In 2023-24, gross irrigated area was 32.71 lakh hectares, net irrigated area was 26.03 lakh hectares and cropping intensity was 1.21. The year was characterised as a drought year.
accepted.tq: Separate the 2023-24 figures from the similar 2022-23 and 2024-25 figures.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The decline in gross irrigated area and net irrigated area in Andhra Pradesh during 2023-24, compared with the preceding year, was respectively
accepted.x: Gross irrigated area declined by 10.53%, while net irrigated area declined by 8.86% in 2023-24.
accepted.tq: Read the paired percentage changes in the same order as the indicators asked.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh during 2023-24, which source accounted for the largest share of Gross Irrigated Area?
accepted.x: Wells and tube wells accounted for the largest share, covering 15.68 lakh hectares or approximately 48% of the GIA.
accepted.tq: Identify the largest category by comparing both the area and percentage share.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding source-wise Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24:

List-I (Source)
a. Wells and tube wells
b. Canals
c. Tanks
d. Others

List-II (Area in lakh hectares)
i. 2.69

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the source-wise distribution of Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24 is NOT correct?
o: Wells and tube wells accounted for approximately 48%.
accepted.x: Other sources accounted for approximately 3%, not 12%. Wells and tube wells, canals and tanks accounted for approximately 48%, 40% and 8%, respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the single percentage that does not fit the source-wise distribution.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which district recorded the largest Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh in 2023-24?
accepted.x: Eluru recorded the largest GIA at 2.39 lakh hectares, followed by Ananthapuramu at 2.04 lakh hectares and Nandyal at 1.98 lakh hectares.
accepted.tq: Use the district ranking and distinguish the highest value from the next two values.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Groundwater accounted for 41% of Gross Irrigated Area in Andhra Pradesh.
2. Andhra Pradesh had approximately 19 lakh bore wells.
3. Groundwater was the smallest source of irrigation in the State in 2023-24.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because groundwater, represented mainly by wells and tube wells, was the largest source of GIA.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed ranking statement after verifying the quantitative statements.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the reported groundwater-irrigated areas in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 29.12 lakh acres gross and 36.63 lakh acres net in 2023-24
36.63 lakh acres net and 41.44 lakh acres gross in 2023-24
29.12 lakh acres net and 41.44 lakh acres gross in 2023-24
41.44 lakh acres net and 29.12 lakh acres gross in 2023-24
accepted.x: Groundwater irrigated 29.12 lakh acres net and 41.44 lakh acres gross in 2023-24. The 36.63 lakh acres figure refers to groundwater-irrigated net area in 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Separate net from gross area and distinguish the year-specific 2024-25 figure.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The importance of tank irrigation in Andhra Pradesh is chiefly associated with which combination of physical conditions?
o: Coastal sand dunes and extensive tidal creeks
Steep Himalayan slopes and glacial deposits
Undulating relief of the peninsular plateau and impervious rocks
Flat alluvial plains and highly permeable rocks
accepted.x: Tank irrigation is important because the peninsular plateau has undulating relief and impervious rocks, which favour the accumulation and storage of water.
accepted.tq: Link the irrigation method to the physical conditions that make it suitable.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Canal irrigation is particularly dominant in which geographical region of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The dry interior plateau away from river valleys
accepted.x: Canals dominate in the Godavari-Krishna delta region, where river water and deltaic conditions support canal irrigation.
accepted.tq: Match the irrigation source with its characteristic regional concentration.
accepted.sec: Irrigation data - GIA/GCA, net irrigated area, source-wise share, top district  [APPSC]

accepted.x: The earlier reported total irrigation potential created was 106.15 lakh acres as on December 2024.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Pattiseema scheme is correct?
o: It lifts Krishna water into the Godavari Right Main Canal for delivery to the Godavari delta.
It lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage.
It transfers water from the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage to the Godavari through a gravity canal.
It diverts Pennar water into the Krishna through the Tungabhadra High Level Canal.
accepted.x: Pattiseema lifts Godavari water into the Polavaram Right Main Canal, which carries it to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage. It is recognised as the first Godavari-Krishna link.
accepted.tq: Trace the direction of flow and identify both the source river and receiving river.
accepted.sec: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages relating to the Pattiseema scheme in chronological order:
A. Commissioning of the scheme
B. Commencement of construction period
C. Completion of the construction period
D. Transfer of approximately 450 TMC of water so far
accepted.x: Construction covered 2014-19, the scheme was commissioned in 2015, and the reported transfer of approximately 450 TMC is a later cumulative outcome. Thus the chronological order is B, C, A, D only if completion is treated as the end of the stated construction period; however, commissioning in 2015 occurred within that period. The exam-relevant sequence of dated milestones is construction commencement in 2014, commissioning in 2015, construction-period end in 2019, followed by the later cumulative transfer.
accepted.tq: Separate the dated construction and commissioning milestones from the later cumulative performance figure.
accepted.sec: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the operational status intended for the Pattiseema scheme?
o: It was intended to operate only during years of normal monsoon rainfall.
It was intended as a temporary arrangement until gravity flow from Polavaram commenced.
It was designed exclusively for supplying drinking water to urban centres.
It was designed as a permanent replacement for Polavaram's gravity flow.
accepted.x: Pattiseema was a temporary scheme intended to function until gravity flow from the Polavaram project became available.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a temporary interim arrangement from a permanent project objective.
accepted.sec: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Pattiseema scheme is correct?
1. It had 24 pumps.
2. It was built during 2014-19.
3. It was commissioned in 2015.
4. It helped keep the Krishna delta supplied during the 2026 El Niño deficit.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Pattiseema had 24 pumps, was built during 2014-19, commissioned in 2015 and helped supply the Krishna delta during the 2026 El Niño deficit.
accepted.tq: Combine structural, chronological and operational facts without confusing commissioning with completion.
accepted.sec: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Approximately how much water had been transferred through the Pattiseema scheme so far, as reported in 2026?
accepted.x: Approximately 450 TMC of water had been transferred through the Pattiseema scheme so far.
accepted.tq: Use the exact cumulative quantity and avoid confusing it with a project capacity figure.
accepted.sec: Pattiseema - type, rivers linked, beneficiaries, temporary nature  [APPSC]
